title.narrative: Core contribution to International Vaccine Institute (IVI) 2023

description.narrative:
Immunization saves millions of lives every year and it the most cost-effective way to prevent disease and improve health. It is estimated that for every USD 1 spent on vaccines USD 16 are saved in future healthcare cost, lost income and lost productivity.
The purpose of the Danish contribution to IVI is to support the organization’s work to achieve its vison of ‘Developing countries free of suffering from infectious diseases’ through the discovery, development and delivery of safe effective and affordable vaccines against infectious diseases that predominantly afflict low- and middle-income countries.

title.narrative: IVI mission to discover, develop and deliver safe, effective and affordable vaccines for global public health, and strengthen AMR-surveillance is accelerated.

1) Development of a vaccine for a pathogen identified by WHO or other disease control organizations as an antimicrobial resistance priority or special pathogen. 2) Collaborative work on global or regional AMR policy, advocacy, science or data with a Danish entity.

target.value:
IVI is expected to have shown progress in each of the Strategic Initiatives in 2026:
1) Current strengths, including vaccine development, epidemiology and surveillance have been amplified
2) IVI operations has expanded into Europe and Africa

actual.value:
1) In 2022-2023, IVI made significant progress on the R&D of three vaccines for variants of Salmonella, a bacteria identified by the WHO as an AMR priority pathogen. These vaccines are: 1. Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV), also known as Vi-DT. 2. A trivalent S. typhi / S. typhimurium / S. enteritidis vaccine (TCV + iNTS). 3. A bivalent S. typhi / S. paratyphi A vaccine (TCV+ Paratyphoid A). In addition, IVI is advancing the development and introduction of vaccines against Streptococcus pyogenes, also known as Group A Strep, a potentially AMR-susceptible pathogen responsible for rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease. The WHO has called for the development of Group A Strep vaccines1, an effort IVI is advancing in its Strep A Vaccine Global Consortium (SAVAC).
2) In 2022-2023, IVI continued collaboration on AMR with its Danish partners, the International Centre for Antimicrobial Resistance Solutions (ICARS), and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU).

title.narrative: IVI operations has expanded into Europe and Asia

1) Significant engagement leading to an increase in state parties and state funders (2 new state parties and 1 new state funder). 2) Establishment of the Global Council comprised of IVI’s State Parties by Q4 2023.

target.value: 1) Significant engagement leading to an increase in state parties and state funders (2 new state parties and 1 new state funder). 2) Establishment of the Global Council comprised of IVI’s State Parties by Q4 2023.

actual.value: 1) Panama successfully completed its accession to IVI as a new state party, marked by a ratification ceremony held in March 2023. Additionally, the governments of Austria, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, and Ghana expressed their intent to join IVI by submitting letters in 2023. 2)On 19 October 2023, IVI successfully initiated the first meeting of its Global Council (IVI GC), a new advisory body comprising representatives from State Parties. The IVI GC is a pivotal platform for State Parties to deliberate on vaccine needs and solutions, foster collaboration and capacity building, advise on the direction of IVI’s programs, and elect State Party representatives to the IVI Board of Trustees.

IVI’s Europe Regional Office in Sweden, Country Office in Austria, and Collaborating Centers in Ethiopia, Ghana, and Madagascar represent IVI’s international expansion and closer collaboration with partners in Europe and Africa on vaccine research, innovation, and capacity-building for global health.

title.narrative: Continued progress in research and development of new vaccines

1) Securing at least 20 new grants or $60M in grant funding in 2023 2) Successful implementation of capacity building and vaccine development assistance programs: a) 1 Tech Transfer and 3 site assessments for vaccine manufacturing, b) biomanufacturing and vaccinology introductory courses (3 courses in 2023).

target.value: 1) Securing at least 20 new grants or $60M in grant funding in 2023 2) Successful implementation of capacity building and vaccine development assistance programs a) 1 Tech Transfer and 3 site assessments for vaccine manufacturing, b) biomanufacturing and vaccinology introductory courses (3 courses in 2023).

actual.value: 1) As of November 2, 2023, the total value of new grants received in 2023 was $63.54 million. 2a) In 2023, IVI completed phases I and II of a technology transfer of simplified oral cholera vaccine (OCV-S) to South Africa’s Biovac Institute. 2b) In 2023, IVI held five courses in biomanufacturing and vaccinology, training over 500 medical professionals, researchers, and vaccine manufacturing technicians, mostly from LMICs.

target.value: Facilitate trainings for professionals from LMIC

actual.value:
In September 2022, IVI’s 21st International Vaccinology Course hosted 200 international trainees at IVI headquarters in Seoul and 20 trainees at Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm with the two sites connected through live streaming. The course included five days of lectures, interactive case studies, and site visits to local vaccine centers. IVI awarded Vaccinology Fellowships to 11 trainees to attend the course at IVI free of charge.
IVI successfully completed the 2022 Introductory Course for Biologics Development and Manufacturing in July to train 106 participants from 24 LMICs and 32 from Korea, and the Introductory Course for Standard Practice (GxP Course) in November to train 200 trainees from 33 LMICs and 42 from Korea.
